94024.company: Mission Trail Waste Systems (serving Los Altos through the City of Los Altos franchised collection program)
94024.bottle: Recycle empty plastic bottles and glass bottles in the blue recycling cart (rinse/empty; caps OK if left on plastic bottles, metal caps can be placed back on glass bottles if secure).
94024.cup: Disposable cups are generally NOT recyclable in the curbside blue cart. Paper coffee cups have plastic lining and go in trash. Plastic cups (e.g., clear party cups) are not accepted in curbside recycling and should go in trash unless a specific drop-off program accepts them.
94024.wine glass: Do NOT put wine glasses in curbside recycling. Put in trash (or reuse/donate if in good condition).
94024.vase: Do NOT put glass vases in curbside recycling. Put in trash (or donate/reuse).
94024.default: Use the blue cart for accepted paper/cardboard, metal cans, and eligible bottles/jars only. Keep materials clean and dry; no bagged recyclables; do not include ceramics, Pyrex, drinking glasses, or other non-container glass. Use green cart for food scraps/yard trimmings if provided, and black/gray cart for landfill items.

90039.company: Los Angeles Sanitation & Environment (LASAN) — Residential Refuse Collection (City of Los Angeles)
90039.bottle: Recycle in the BLUE bin if empty and dry (plastic bottles and glass bottles/jars). Put caps/lids back on plastic bottles when possible; do not bag recyclables.
90039.cup: Disposable cups: If plastic (#1–#7) and empty/clean/dry, place in the BLUE bin. Paper cups (including hot/coffee cups) are generally NOT accepted in curbside recycling due to plastic lining—place in the BLACK bin unless specifically labeled and accepted by a separate program.
90039.wine glass: Do NOT place in the BLUE bin. Wine glasses (drinking glass/tempered glass) are not accepted with container glass—wrap and place in the BLACK bin (trash) to prevent contamination and injury.
90039.vase: Do NOT place in the BLUE bin if it is a decorative glass vase (non-container glass). Place in the BLACK bin (trash) or reuse/donate if in good condition.
90039.default: For ZIP 90039 (City of Los Angeles): Use the BLUE bin for empty, clean, dry bottles/jars and other accepted recyclables (mixed paper/cardboard, metal cans/foil, rigid plastics). Keep items loose (no bags), and keep food/liquid out. Non-container glass (drinkware, vases, ceramics) goes in the BLACK bin (trash). GREEN bin is for yard trimmings/organics where provided.

93923.company: Carmel Area Wastewater District / Monterey Peninsula Waste Management District (MPWMD) — serviced by Monterey Disposal Service (WM)
93923.bottle: Recycle empty plastic bottles and glass bottles in the curbside recycling cart (place loose, not bagged). Rinse/empty; keep caps on plastic bottles; remove non-bottle pumps/sprayers.
93923.cup: Disposable cups: Plastic cups generally go in the recycling cart only if accepted as rigid plastic by the local program; otherwise place in trash. Paper cups (coffee cups) are typically NOT recyclable due to plastic lining—put in trash unless specifically accepted by the local hauler. When in doubt for Carmel/Monterey Peninsula programs, trash paper coffee cups and most single-use plastic cups.
93923.wine glass: Do NOT put wine glasses in curbside recycling. Put in trash (or take to a specialty facility if available).
93923.vase: Do NOT put glass vases in curbside recycling. Put in trash or donate/reuse if in good condition.
93923.default: Carmel (93923) curbside recycling typically accepts common containers like bottles, jars, cans, clean paper and cardboard. Do not include ceramics, drinking glasses, window glass, mirrors, vases, or Pyrex; keep recyclables empty/clean and loose (no bagged recyclables). When uncertain, favor trash to avoid contaminating the recycling stream.
